About Liberty CTI

Built by intelligence officers for leaders who must decide under pressure.

Liberty CTI was founded by two career U.S. Air Force intelligence officers with nearly six decades of combined national-security service, spent turning adversary behavior, geopolitical change, and operational uncertainty into advice senior leaders could use.

Nearly 60 years of combined service

Enlisted linguists who became intelligence officers and commanders.

White House, NSC, and the Pentagon

Situation Room, National Security Council, and senior Defense staff.

Command

A cyber intelligence organization and a training squadron, both in Texas.

Why We Built This

We saw the gap. We built for decisions.

Across our careers, we watched technically accurate reporting reach senior leaders in formats that still required translation. The facts were often right. The decision relevance was left to the reader. Much of the market is built for security teams, not for boards and executive operators. It answers “what happened?” when leadership is asking what changed, what decision it affects, and what should be documented now.

Texas energy, financial, healthcare, and defense organizations face real cyber and geopolitical pressure, but the leaders responsible for them often lack a usable external warning function before decisions become evidence. Liberty CTI was built to fill that gap with Strategic Cyber Intelligence shaped by national-security experience.

In military vernacular, a mustang is a former enlisted service member who becomes an officer, shaped by real work rather than institutional polish. That identity sits at the center of Liberty CTI.

What Liberty CTI Is

Strategic Cyber Intelligence. Judgment, not just information.

Most cyber reporting tells you what happened. Liberty CTI tells you what changed, what decision it affects, and what should be documented before a crisis forces the call. Our judgments are published, kept, and graded on The Track Record.

What it is not

  • Not a security operations center, managed detection, or incident response.
  • Not penetration testing or a technical threat-intelligence feed.
  • Not a compliance or audit firm, and not a replacement for your CISO or counsel.
  • We use open sources and the information clients authorize, never classified or unlawfully obtained material.

Our View

Warning without a decision record is fragile.

Texas leaders operate in an environment where cyber risk no longer sits neatly inside the security function. Geopolitical competition, criminal ecosystems, supply-chain concentration, and cross-sector dependency now shape operating decisions across infrastructure, finance, healthcare, and defense.

The practical question is whether your organization can show it received warning, understood the risk, and documented action before a crisis forced the decision. The record matters when regulators, insurers, shareholders, or courts ask what leadership knew and what it did next.

See how we think. Then test how your leadership decides.
